# Worked TAP workflows (from the Schema Explorer)

Eight end-to-end ADQL workflows (4 science cases × LSST/ZTF), copied from the **alerce_tap Schema Explorer** ([artifact](https://claude.ai/artifact/JEpEyijsTpD1y83ut7Zia7)). The explorer re-runs every query daily; snapshot of 2026-11-19. Each follows the same pattern: look up ids → look up bands/features → select candidates → filter by features → light curve (detections, forced photometry) → crossmatch.

The ids written in the queries (classifier_id, class_id, feature ids, the example oid) were correct on that date. **Resolve them by name at runtime** (step 1–2 of each workflow) before reusing a query; class ids are per classifier and feature ids differ per survey.

## Supernovae

### Supernovae · LSST

Find fresh LSST supernova candidates from the Rubin stamp classifier, characterise them with light-curve features, and download one candidate’s light curve, forced photometry and crossmatches.

**1. Look up the ids** (≈1 s · 6 rows)

The survey id (sid) and the classifier and class ids for “SN”. This variant uses sid = 1 (LSST DIA objects), the newest Rubin stamp classifier (classifier_id = 3) and class_id = 0.


```sql
SELECT s.sid, s.survey_name, c.classifier_id, c.classifier_name,
       c.classifier_version, t.class_id, t.class_name
FROM alerce_tap.classifier AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.taxonomy AS t ON t.classifier_id = c.classifier_id
JOIN alerce_tap.sid_lut AS s ON s.tid = c.tid
WHERE t.class_name IN ('SN')
ORDER BY s.sid, c.classifier_id, t.class_id
```
→ 6 row(s) on 2026-11-19: sid, survey_name, classifier_id, classifier_name, classifier_version, class_id, class_name

**2. Look up bands and features** (≈1 s each · 6 / 3 / 3 rows)

LSST bands and the ids of the supernova-model (SPM) features. Feature ids differ between surveys, so always look them up with sid. In the feature table, band 0 means “no band” and two-digit values such as 12 mean a band combination.

*Bands*
```sql
SELECT band, band_name, band_order
FROM alerce_tap.band
WHERE sid = 1
ORDER BY band_order
```
→ 6 row(s) on 2026-11-19: band, band_name, band_order

*Features used*
```sql
SELECT feature_id, feature_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_name_lut
WHERE sid = 1 AND feature_name IN ('SPM_tau_rise', 'SPM_tau_fall', 'SPM_A')
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: feature_id, feature_name

*Feature versions*
```sql
SELECT version_id, version_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_version_lut
WHERE sid = 1
```
→ 5 row(s) on 2026-11-19: version_id, version_name

**3. Find SN candidates** (≈1 s · 10 rows)

Top Rubin stamp-classifier SN candidates with probability > 0.8.


```sql
SELECT TOP 10 p.oid, p.probability, o.meanra, o.meandec, o.firstmjd, o.lastmjd, o.n_det
FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
JOIN alerce_tap.object AS o ON o.oid = p.oid AND o.sid = p.sid
WHERE p.sid = 1 AND p.classifier_id = 3 AND p.class_id = 0
  AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
ORDER BY p.probability DESC
```
→ 10 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, meanra, meandec, firstmjd, lastmjd, n_det

**4. Search by features** (≈1 s · 57 rows)

Rise time, fall time and amplitude of the parametric supernova model (SPM) per band, for the top 20 candidates: use them to tell fast from slow transients.


```sql
SELECT c.oid, c.probability, n.feature_name, b.band_name, f.feature_value
FROM (SELECT TOP 20 p.oid, p.sid, p.probability
      FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
      WHERE p.sid = 1 AND p.classifier_id = 3 AND p.class_id = 0
        AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
      ORDER BY p.probability DESC) AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.feature AS f ON f.oid = c.oid AND f.sid = c.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.feature_name_lut AS n ON n.sid = f.sid AND n.feature_id = f.feature_id
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE n.feature_name IN ('SPM_tau_rise', 'SPM_tau_fall', 'SPM_A')
ORDER BY c.probability DESC, n.feature_name, b.band_order
```
→ 50 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, feature_name, band_name, feature_value

**5. Light curve: detections** (≈1 s · 5 rows)

Difference flux (psfflux) and total flux (scienceflux) in nJy, with Rubin’s reliability score.


```sql
SELECT d.mjd, b.band_name, x.psfflux, x.psffluxerr, x.scienceflux, x.sciencefluxerr, x.reliability
FROM alerce_tap.detection AS d
JOIN alerce_tap.lsst_detection AS x
  ON x.oid = d.oid AND x.measurement_id = d.measurement_id AND x.sid = d.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = d.sid AND b.band = d.band
WHERE d.oid = 170595943059554358 AND d.sid = 1
ORDER BY d.mjd
```
→ 5 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, psfflux, psffluxerr, scienceflux, sciencefluxerr, reliability

**6. Light curve: forced photometry** (≈1 s · 4 rows)

Fluxes measured at the object position in every visit sent with the alerts, including epochs without a detection.


```sql
SELECT f.mjd, b.band_name, x.psfflux, x.psffluxerr, x.scienceflux, x.sciencefluxerr
FROM alerce_tap.forced_photometry AS f
JOIN alerce_tap.lsst_forced_photometry AS x
  ON x.oid = f.oid AND x.measurement_id = f.measurement_id AND x.sid = f.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE f.oid = 170595943059554358 AND f.sid = 1
ORDER BY f.mjd
```
→ 4 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, psfflux, psffluxerr, scienceflux, sciencefluxerr

**7. Crossmatches** (≈1 s · 1 row)

AllWISE and Gaia DR3 counterparts within the match radius; for a supernova this is often the host galaxy, when one is matched.


```sql
SELECT c.catalog_name, x.oid_catalog, x.dist,
       a.w1mpro, a.w2mpro, a.w1mpro - a.w2mpro AS w1_w2,
       g.phot_g_mean_mag, g.bp_rp, g.parallax,
       g.phot_variable_flag, g.in_qso_candidates
FROM alerce_tap.xmatch AS x
JOIN alerce_tap.catalog_id_lut AS c ON c.catid = x.catid
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.allwise AS a
  ON x.catid = 0 AND a.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.gaiadr3_source AS g
  ON x.catid = 1 AND g.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
WHERE x.oid = 170595943059554358 AND x.sid = 1
```
→ 1 row(s) on 2026-11-19: catalog_name, oid_catalog, dist, w1mpro, w2mpro, w1_w2, phot_g_mean_mag, bp_rp, parallax, phot_variable_flag, in_qso_candidates

### Supernovae · ZTF

Find ZTF type Ia supernova candidates from the light-curve classifier, characterise them with light-curve features, and download one candidate’s light curve, forced photometry and crossmatches.

**1. Look up the ids** (≈1 s · 14 rows)

The survey id and the classifier and class ids for supernova classes. This variant uses sid = 0 (ZTF), the flat light-curve classifier (classifier_id = 5) and class SNIa (class_id = 18); the stamp classifiers have a generic SN class instead.


```sql
SELECT s.sid, s.survey_name, c.classifier_id, c.classifier_name,
       c.classifier_version, t.class_id, t.class_name
FROM alerce_tap.classifier AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.taxonomy AS t ON t.classifier_id = c.classifier_id
JOIN alerce_tap.sid_lut AS s ON s.tid = c.tid
WHERE t.class_name IN ('SN', 'SNIa', 'SNII', 'SESN', 'SLSN')
ORDER BY s.sid, c.classifier_id, t.class_id
```
→ 14 row(s) on 2026-11-19: sid, survey_name, classifier_id, classifier_name, classifier_version, class_id, class_name

**2. Look up bands and features** (≈1 s each · 3 / 3 / 2 rows)

ZTF bands and the ids of the supernova-model (SPM) features. Feature ids differ between surveys, so always look them up with sid.

*Bands*
```sql
SELECT band, band_name, band_order
FROM alerce_tap.band
WHERE sid = 0
ORDER BY band_order
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: band, band_name, band_order

*Features used*
```sql
SELECT feature_id, feature_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_name_lut
WHERE sid = 0 AND feature_name IN ('SPM_tau_rise', 'SPM_tau_fall', 'SPM_A')
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: feature_id, feature_name

*Feature versions*
```sql
SELECT version_id, version_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_version_lut
WHERE sid = 0
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: version_id, version_name

**3. Find SNIa candidates** (≈1 s · 10 rows)

Top light-curve-classifier SNIa candidates with probability > 0.8.


```sql
SELECT TOP 10 p.oid, p.probability, o.meanra, o.meandec, o.firstmjd, o.lastmjd, o.n_det
FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
JOIN alerce_tap.object AS o ON o.oid = p.oid AND o.sid = p.sid
WHERE p.sid = 0 AND p.classifier_id = 5 AND p.class_id = 18
  AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
ORDER BY p.probability DESC
```
→ 10 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, meanra, meandec, firstmjd, lastmjd, n_det

**4. Search by features** (≈1 s · 120 rows)

Rise time, fall time and amplitude of the parametric supernova model (SPM) in g and r, for the top 20 candidates.


```sql
SELECT c.oid, c.probability, n.feature_name, b.band_name, f.feature_value
FROM (SELECT TOP 20 p.oid, p.sid, p.probability
      FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
      WHERE p.sid = 0 AND p.classifier_id = 5 AND p.class_id = 18
        AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
      ORDER BY p.probability DESC) AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.feature AS f ON f.oid = c.oid AND f.sid = c.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.feature_name_lut AS n ON n.sid = f.sid AND n.feature_id = f.feature_id
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE n.feature_name IN ('SPM_tau_rise', 'SPM_tau_fall', 'SPM_A')
ORDER BY c.probability DESC, n.feature_name, b.band_order
```
→ 50 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, feature_name, band_name, feature_value

**5. Light curve: detections** (≈1 s · 30 rows)

Difference magnitudes (magpsf) and corrected apparent magnitudes (magpsf_corr).


```sql
SELECT d.mjd, b.band_name, x.magpsf, x.sigmapsf, x.magpsf_corr, x.sigmapsf_corr
FROM alerce_tap.detection AS d
JOIN alerce_tap.ztf_detection AS x
  ON x.oid = d.oid AND x.measurement_id = d.measurement_id
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = d.sid AND b.band = d.band
WHERE d.oid = 36028957656154092 AND d.sid = 0
ORDER BY d.mjd
```
→ 30 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, magpsf, sigmapsf, magpsf_corr, sigmapsf_corr

**6. Light curve: forced photometry** (≈1 s · 54 rows)

ZTF forced photometry at the object position, including epochs before the first detection.


```sql
SELECT f.mjd, b.band_name, x.mag, x.e_mag, x.mag_corr, x.e_mag_corr
FROM alerce_tap.forced_photometry AS f
JOIN alerce_tap.ztf_forced_photometry AS x
  ON x.oid = f.oid AND x.measurement_id = f.measurement_id
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE f.oid = 36028957656154092 AND f.sid = 0
ORDER BY f.mjd
```
→ 50 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, mag, e_mag, mag_corr, e_mag_corr

**7. Crossmatches** (≈1 s · 1 row)

Catalog counterparts at the transient position. Most supernovae have none, because the match is made at the supernova position, not the host’s.


```sql
SELECT c.catalog_name, x.oid_catalog, x.dist,
       a.w1mpro, a.w2mpro, a.w1mpro - a.w2mpro AS w1_w2,
       g.phot_g_mean_mag, g.bp_rp, g.parallax,
       g.phot_variable_flag, g.in_qso_candidates
FROM alerce_tap.xmatch AS x
JOIN alerce_tap.catalog_id_lut AS c ON c.catid = x.catid
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.allwise AS a
  ON x.catid = 0 AND a.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.gaiadr3_source AS g
  ON x.catid = 1 AND g.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
WHERE x.oid = 36028957656154092 AND x.sid = 0
```
→ 1 row(s) on 2026-11-19: catalog_name, oid_catalog, dist, w1mpro, w2mpro, w1_w2, phot_g_mean_mag, bp_rp, parallax, phot_variable_flag, in_qso_candidates

## AGN

### AGN · LSST

Find LSST AGN candidates from the Rubin stamp classifier, keep those with AGN-like mid-infrared colours, and download one object’s light curve, forced photometry and crossmatches.

**1. Look up the ids** (≈1 s · 12 rows)

Survey, classifier and class ids for AGN-like classes. This variant uses sid = 1 (LSST), classifier_id = 3 (Rubin stamp classifier) and class AGN (class_id = 1). Class ids are numbered per classifier.


```sql
SELECT s.sid, s.survey_name, c.classifier_id, c.classifier_name,
       c.classifier_version, t.class_id, t.class_name
FROM alerce_tap.classifier AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.taxonomy AS t ON t.classifier_id = c.classifier_id
JOIN alerce_tap.sid_lut AS s ON s.tid = c.tid
WHERE t.class_name IN ('AGN', 'QSO', 'Blazar')
ORDER BY s.sid, c.classifier_id, t.class_id
```
→ 12 row(s) on 2026-11-19: sid, survey_name, classifier_id, classifier_name, classifier_version, class_id, class_name

**2. Look up bands and features** (≈1 s each · 6 / 3 / 3 rows)

LSST bands and the feature ids for W1−W2, the damped-random-walk timescale and the excess variance. W1−W2 is stored with band 0 (no band).

*Bands*
```sql
SELECT band, band_name, band_order
FROM alerce_tap.band
WHERE sid = 1
ORDER BY band_order
```
→ 6 row(s) on 2026-11-19: band, band_name, band_order

*Features used*
```sql
SELECT feature_id, feature_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_name_lut
WHERE sid = 1 AND feature_name IN ('W1-W2', 'GP_DRW_tau', 'ExcessVar')
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: feature_id, feature_name

*Feature versions*
```sql
SELECT version_id, version_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_version_lut
WHERE sid = 1
```
→ 5 row(s) on 2026-11-19: version_id, version_name

**3. Find AGN candidates** (≈1 s · 10 rows)

Top Rubin stamp-classifier AGN candidates with probability > 0.8.


```sql
SELECT TOP 10 p.oid, p.probability, o.meanra, o.meandec, o.firstmjd, o.lastmjd, o.n_det
FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
JOIN alerce_tap.object AS o ON o.oid = p.oid AND o.sid = p.sid
WHERE p.sid = 1 AND p.classifier_id = 3 AND p.class_id = 1
  AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
ORDER BY p.probability DESC
```
→ 10 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, meanra, meandec, firstmjd, lastmjd, n_det

**4. Search by features** (≈2 s · 33 rows)

Among the top 200 AGN candidates, keep those with W1 − W2 > 0.8, the classic mid-infrared AGN selection.


```sql
SELECT c.oid, c.probability, f.feature_value AS w1_w2
FROM (SELECT TOP 200 p.oid, p.sid, p.probability
      FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
      WHERE p.sid = 1 AND p.classifier_id = 3 AND p.class_id = 1
        AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
      ORDER BY p.probability DESC) AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.feature AS f ON f.oid = c.oid AND f.sid = c.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.feature_name_lut AS n ON n.sid = f.sid AND n.feature_id = f.feature_id
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE n.feature_name IN ('W1-W2') AND f.feature_value > 0.8
ORDER BY f.feature_value DESC
```
→ 37 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, w1_w2

**5. Light curve: detections** (≈1 s · 2 rows)

Difference and total fluxes in nJy.


```sql
SELECT d.mjd, b.band_name, x.psfflux, x.psffluxerr, x.scienceflux, x.sciencefluxerr, x.reliability
FROM alerce_tap.detection AS d
JOIN alerce_tap.lsst_detection AS x
  ON x.oid = d.oid AND x.measurement_id = d.measurement_id AND x.sid = d.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = d.sid AND b.band = d.band
WHERE d.oid = 170631093046742856 AND d.sid = 1
ORDER BY d.mjd
```
→ 2 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, psfflux, psffluxerr, scienceflux, sciencefluxerr, reliability

**6. Light curve: forced photometry** (≈1 s · 1 row)

Forced fluxes at the object position.


```sql
SELECT f.mjd, b.band_name, x.psfflux, x.psffluxerr, x.scienceflux, x.sciencefluxerr
FROM alerce_tap.forced_photometry AS f
JOIN alerce_tap.lsst_forced_photometry AS x
  ON x.oid = f.oid AND x.measurement_id = f.measurement_id AND x.sid = f.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE f.oid = 170631093046742856 AND f.sid = 1
ORDER BY f.mjd
```
→ 1 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, psfflux, psffluxerr, scienceflux, sciencefluxerr

**7. Crossmatches** (≈1 s · 2 rows)

AllWISE mid-infrared colour and Gaia DR3 flags.


```sql
SELECT c.catalog_name, x.oid_catalog, x.dist,
       a.w1mpro, a.w2mpro, a.w1mpro - a.w2mpro AS w1_w2,
       g.phot_g_mean_mag, g.bp_rp, g.parallax,
       g.phot_variable_flag, g.in_qso_candidates
FROM alerce_tap.xmatch AS x
JOIN alerce_tap.catalog_id_lut AS c ON c.catid = x.catid
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.allwise AS a
  ON x.catid = 0 AND a.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.gaiadr3_source AS g
  ON x.catid = 1 AND g.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
WHERE x.oid = 170631093046742856 AND x.sid = 1
```
→ 2 row(s) on 2026-11-19: catalog_name, oid_catalog, dist, w1mpro, w2mpro, w1_w2, phot_g_mean_mag, bp_rp, parallax, phot_variable_flag, in_qso_candidates

### AGN · ZTF

Find ZTF quasar candidates from the light-curve classifier, keep those with AGN-like mid-infrared colours, and download one object’s light curve, forced photometry and crossmatches.

**1. Look up the ids** (≈1 s · 12 rows)

Class ids are numbered per classifier: QSO is class 10 in the flat light-curve classifier (classifier_id = 5) but class 4 in its stochastic branch (8). This variant uses sid = 0 (ZTF), classifier_id = 5, class_id = 10.


```sql
SELECT s.sid, s.survey_name, c.classifier_id, c.classifier_name,
       c.classifier_version, t.class_id, t.class_name
FROM alerce_tap.classifier AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.taxonomy AS t ON t.classifier_id = c.classifier_id
JOIN alerce_tap.sid_lut AS s ON s.tid = c.tid
WHERE t.class_name IN ('AGN', 'QSO', 'Blazar')
ORDER BY s.sid, c.classifier_id, t.class_id
```
→ 12 row(s) on 2026-11-19: sid, survey_name, classifier_id, classifier_name, classifier_version, class_id, class_name

**2. Look up bands and features** (≈1 s each · 3 / 3 / 2 rows)

ZTF bands and the feature ids for W1−W2, the damped-random-walk timescale and the excess variance. W1−W2 is stored with band 0 (no band).

*Bands*
```sql
SELECT band, band_name, band_order
FROM alerce_tap.band
WHERE sid = 0
ORDER BY band_order
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: band, band_name, band_order

*Features used*
```sql
SELECT feature_id, feature_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_name_lut
WHERE sid = 0 AND feature_name IN ('W1-W2', 'GP_DRW_tau', 'ExcessVar')
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: feature_id, feature_name

*Feature versions*
```sql
SELECT version_id, version_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_version_lut
WHERE sid = 0
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: version_id, version_name

**3. Find QSO candidates** (≈1 s · 10 rows)

Top light-curve-classifier QSO candidates with probability > 0.8 (AGN is class 0, Blazar 1).


```sql
SELECT TOP 10 p.oid, p.probability, o.meanra, o.meandec, o.firstmjd, o.lastmjd, o.n_det
FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
JOIN alerce_tap.object AS o ON o.oid = p.oid AND o.sid = p.sid
WHERE p.sid = 0 AND p.classifier_id = 5 AND p.class_id = 10
  AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
ORDER BY p.probability DESC
```
→ 10 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, meanra, meandec, firstmjd, lastmjd, n_det

**4. Search by features** (≈1 s · 50 rows)

Among the top 50 QSO candidates, keep those with W1 − W2 > 0.8, the classic mid-infrared AGN selection.


```sql
SELECT c.oid, c.probability, f.feature_value AS w1_w2
FROM (SELECT TOP 50 p.oid, p.sid, p.probability
      FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
      WHERE p.sid = 0 AND p.classifier_id = 5 AND p.class_id = 10
        AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
      ORDER BY p.probability DESC) AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.feature AS f ON f.oid = c.oid AND f.sid = c.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.feature_name_lut AS n ON n.sid = f.sid AND n.feature_id = f.feature_id
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE n.feature_name IN ('W1-W2') AND f.feature_value > 0.8
ORDER BY f.feature_value DESC
```
→ 50 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, w1_w2

**5. Light curve: detections** (≈1 s · 88 rows)

Difference magnitudes and corrected apparent magnitudes (magpsf_corr), the right column for AGN variability.


```sql
SELECT d.mjd, b.band_name, x.magpsf, x.sigmapsf, x.magpsf_corr, x.sigmapsf_corr
FROM alerce_tap.detection AS d
JOIN alerce_tap.ztf_detection AS x
  ON x.oid = d.oid AND x.measurement_id = d.measurement_id

ORDER BY d.mjd
```
→ 50 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, magpsf, sigmapsf, magpsf_corr, sigmapsf_corr

**6. Light curve: forced photometry** (≈1 s · 79 rows)

ZTF forced photometry at the object position (mag_corr = apparent magnitude).


```sql
SELECT f.mjd, b.band_name, x.mag, x.e_mag, x.mag_corr, x.e_mag_corr
FROM alerce_tap.forced_photometry AS f
JOIN alerce_tap.ztf_forced_photometry AS x

```
→ 50 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, mag, e_mag, mag_corr, e_mag_corr

**7. Crossmatches** (≈1 s · 2 rows)

AllWISE mid-infrared colour and Gaia DR3 flags.


```sql
SELECT c.catalog_name, x.oid_catalog, x.dist,
       a.w1mpro, a.w2mpro, a.w1mpro - a.w2mpro AS w1_w2,
       g.phot_g_mean_mag, g.bp_rp, g.parallax,
       g.phot_variable_flag, g.in_qso_candidates
FROM alerce_tap.xmatch AS x
JOIN alerce_tap.catalog_id_lut AS c ON c.catid = x.catid
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.allwise AS a
  ON x.catid = 0 AND a.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.gaiadr3_source AS g
  ON x.catid = 1 AND g.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
WHERE x.oid = 36028957662234449 AND x.sid = 0
```
→ 2 row(s) on 2026-11-19: catalog_name, oid_catalog, dist, w1mpro, w2mpro, w1_w2, phot_g_mean_mag, bp_rp, parallax, phot_variable_flag, in_qso_candidates

## Variable stars

### Variable stars · LSST

Find LSST variable-star candidates from the Rubin stamp classifier, read their periods, and download one star’s light curve, forced photometry and crossmatches.

**1. Look up the ids** (≈1 s · 20 rows)

Survey, classifier and class ids for variable-star classes. The Rubin stamp classifier has one generic class VS (class_id = 2); the detailed periodic classes exist only in the ZTF light-curve classifier.


```sql
SELECT s.sid, s.survey_name, c.classifier_id, c.classifier_name,
       c.classifier_version, t.class_id, t.class_name
FROM alerce_tap.classifier AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.taxonomy AS t ON t.classifier_id = c.classifier_id
JOIN alerce_tap.sid_lut AS s ON s.tid = c.tid
WHERE t.class_name IN ('VS', 'RRLab', 'RRLc', 'CEP', 'DSCT', 'EA', 'EB/EW', 'LPV')
ORDER BY s.sid, c.classifier_id, t.class_id
```
→ 20 row(s) on 2026-11-19: sid, survey_name, classifier_id, classifier_name, classifier_version, class_id, class_name

**2. Look up bands and features** (≈1 s each · 6 / 3 / 3 rows)

LSST bands and the feature ids for the multiband period, amplitude and period significance (PPE). In LSST the multiband period is stored with band 0.

*Bands*
```sql
SELECT band, band_name, band_order
FROM alerce_tap.band
WHERE sid = 1
ORDER BY band_order
```
→ 6 row(s) on 2026-11-19: band, band_name, band_order

*Features used*
```sql
SELECT feature_id, feature_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_name_lut
WHERE sid = 1 AND feature_name IN ('Multiband_period', 'Amplitude', 'PPE')
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: feature_id, feature_name

*Feature versions*
```sql
SELECT version_id, version_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_version_lut
WHERE sid = 1
```
→ 5 row(s) on 2026-11-19: version_id, version_name

**3. Find VS candidates** (≈1 s · 10 rows)

Top Rubin stamp-classifier VS candidates with probability > 0.8.


```sql
SELECT TOP 10 p.oid, p.probability, o.meanra, o.meandec, o.firstmjd, o.lastmjd, o.n_det
FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
JOIN alerce_tap.object AS o ON o.oid = p.oid AND o.sid = p.sid
WHERE p.sid = 1 AND p.classifier_id = 3 AND p.class_id = 2
  AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
ORDER BY p.probability DESC
```
→ 10 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, meanra, meandec, firstmjd, lastmjd, n_det

**4. Search by features** (≈1 s · 6 rows)

Periods of the top 200 VS candidates. Few LSST light curves are long enough for a period yet, so expect only a handful of rows.


```sql
SELECT c.oid, c.probability, f.feature_value AS period_days
FROM (SELECT TOP 200 p.oid, p.sid, p.probability
      FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
      WHERE p.sid = 1 AND p.classifier_id = 3 AND p.class_id = 2
        AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
      ORDER BY p.probability DESC) AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.feature AS f ON f.oid = c.oid AND f.sid = c.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.feature_name_lut AS n ON n.sid = f.sid AND n.feature_id = f.feature_id
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE n.feature_name IN ('Multiband_period')
ORDER BY c.probability DESC
```
→ 5 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, period_days

**5. Light curve: detections** (≈1 s · 18 rows)

Difference and total fluxes in nJy; fold them on the period from step 4.


```sql
SELECT d.mjd, b.band_name, x.psfflux, x.psffluxerr, x.scienceflux, x.sciencefluxerr, x.reliability
FROM alerce_tap.detection AS d
JOIN alerce_tap.lsst_detection AS x
  ON x.oid = d.oid AND x.measurement_id = d.measurement_id AND x.sid = d.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = d.sid AND b.band = d.band
WHERE d.oid = 170028489278226435 AND d.sid = 1
ORDER BY d.mjd
```
→ 18 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, psfflux, psffluxerr, scienceflux, sciencefluxerr, reliability

**6. Light curve: forced photometry** (≈1 s · 93 rows)

Forced fluxes at the object position.


```sql
SELECT f.mjd, b.band_name, x.psfflux, x.psffluxerr, x.scienceflux, x.sciencefluxerr
FROM alerce_tap.forced_photometry AS f
JOIN alerce_tap.lsst_forced_photometry AS x
  ON x.oid = f.oid AND x.measurement_id = f.measurement_id AND x.sid = f.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE f.oid = 170028489278226435 AND f.sid = 1
ORDER BY f.mjd
```
→ 50 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, psfflux, psffluxerr, scienceflux, sciencefluxerr

**7. Crossmatches** (≈1 s · 2 rows)

AllWISE and Gaia DR3 counterparts: parallax, colour and variability flag.


```sql
SELECT c.catalog_name, x.oid_catalog, x.dist,
       a.w1mpro, a.w2mpro, a.w1mpro - a.w2mpro AS w1_w2,
       g.phot_g_mean_mag, g.bp_rp, g.parallax,
       g.phot_variable_flag, g.in_qso_candidates
FROM alerce_tap.xmatch AS x
JOIN alerce_tap.catalog_id_lut AS c ON c.catid = x.catid
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.allwise AS a
  ON x.catid = 0 AND a.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.gaiadr3_source AS g
  ON x.catid = 1 AND g.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
WHERE x.oid = 170028489278226435 AND x.sid = 1
```
→ 2 row(s) on 2026-11-19: catalog_name, oid_catalog, dist, w1mpro, w2mpro, w1_w2, phot_g_mean_mag, bp_rp, parallax, phot_variable_flag, in_qso_candidates

### Variable stars · ZTF

Find ZTF RR Lyrae (ab) stars from the light-curve classifier, keep those with RR Lyrae periods, and download one star’s light curve, forced photometry and crossmatches.

**1. Look up the ids** (≈1 s · 20 rows)

Periodic classes in the light-curve classifier. This variant uses sid = 0 (ZTF), classifier_id = 5 (flat classifier), class_id = 11 (RRLab); the periodic branch (9) numbers its classes differently.


```sql
SELECT s.sid, s.survey_name, c.classifier_id, c.classifier_name,
       c.classifier_version, t.class_id, t.class_name
FROM alerce_tap.classifier AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.taxonomy AS t ON t.classifier_id = c.classifier_id
JOIN alerce_tap.sid_lut AS s ON s.tid = c.tid
WHERE t.class_name IN ('VS', 'RRLab', 'RRLc', 'CEP', 'DSCT', 'EA', 'EB/EW', 'LPV')
ORDER BY s.sid, c.classifier_id, t.class_id
```
→ 20 row(s) on 2026-11-19: sid, survey_name, classifier_id, classifier_name, classifier_version, class_id, class_name

**2. Look up bands and features** (≈1 s each · 3 / 3 / 2 rows)

ZTF bands and the feature ids for the multiband period, amplitude and period significance (PPE). In ZTF the multiband period uses band 12 (g+r together).

*Bands*
```sql
SELECT band, band_name, band_order
FROM alerce_tap.band
WHERE sid = 0
ORDER BY band_order
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: band, band_name, band_order

*Features used*
```sql
SELECT feature_id, feature_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_name_lut
WHERE sid = 0 AND feature_name IN ('Multiband_period', 'Amplitude', 'PPE')
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: feature_id, feature_name

*Feature versions*
```sql
SELECT version_id, version_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_version_lut
WHERE sid = 0
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: version_id, version_name

**3. Find RR Lyrae candidates** (≈1 s · 10 rows)

Top light-curve-classifier RRLab candidates with probability > 0.8 (RRLc 12, CEP 2, DSCT 4, EA 5, EB/EW 6, LPV 7).


```sql
SELECT TOP 10 p.oid, p.probability, o.meanra, o.meandec, o.firstmjd, o.lastmjd, o.n_det
FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
JOIN alerce_tap.object AS o ON o.oid = p.oid AND o.sid = p.sid
WHERE p.sid = 0 AND p.classifier_id = 5 AND p.class_id = 11
  AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
ORDER BY p.probability DESC
```
→ 10 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, meanra, meandec, firstmjd, lastmjd, n_det

**4. Search by features** (≈2 s · 50 rows)

Among the top 50 RRLab candidates, keep those with a multiband period between 0.4 and 0.9 days, the RR Lyrae ab range.


```sql
SELECT c.oid, c.probability, f.feature_value AS period_days
FROM (SELECT TOP 50 p.oid, p.sid, p.probability
      FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
      WHERE p.sid = 0 AND p.classifier_id = 5 AND p.class_id = 11
        AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
      ORDER BY p.probability DESC) AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.feature AS f ON f.oid = c.oid AND f.sid = c.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.feature_name_lut AS n ON n.sid = f.sid AND n.feature_id = f.feature_id
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE n.feature_name IN ('Multiband_period') AND f.feature_value BETWEEN 0.4 AND 0.9
ORDER BY c.probability DESC
```
→ 50 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, period_days

**5. Light curve: detections** (≈2 s · 488 rows)

Use magpsf_corr (apparent magnitude) to fold the light curve on the period from step 4.


```sql
SELECT d.mjd, b.band_name, x.magpsf, x.sigmapsf, x.magpsf_corr, x.sigmapsf_corr
FROM alerce_tap.detection AS d
JOIN alerce_tap.ztf_detection AS x
  ON x.oid = d.oid AND x.measurement_id = d.measurement_id
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = d.sid AND b.band = d.band
WHERE d.oid = 36028941607751853 AND d.sid = 0
ORDER BY d.mjd
```
→ 50 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, magpsf, sigmapsf, magpsf_corr, sigmapsf_corr

**6. Light curve: forced photometry** (≈1 s · 185 rows)

More epochs at the object position, useful to fill the phased light curve.


```sql
SELECT f.mjd, b.band_name, x.mag, x.e_mag, x.mag_corr, x.e_mag_corr
FROM alerce_tap.forced_photometry AS f
JOIN alerce_tap.ztf_forced_photometry AS x
  ON x.oid = f.oid AND x.measurement_id = f.measurement_id
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE f.oid = 36028941607751853 AND f.sid = 0
ORDER BY f.mjd
```
→ 50 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, mag, e_mag, mag_corr, e_mag_corr

**7. Crossmatches** (≈1 s · 1 row)

Gaia DR3 parallax, colour and variability flag.


```sql
SELECT c.catalog_name, x.oid_catalog, x.dist,
       a.w1mpro, a.w2mpro, a.w1mpro - a.w2mpro AS w1_w2,
       g.phot_g_mean_mag, g.bp_rp, g.parallax,
       g.phot_variable_flag, g.in_qso_candidates
FROM alerce_tap.xmatch AS x
JOIN alerce_tap.catalog_id_lut AS c ON c.catid = x.catid
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.allwise AS a
  ON x.catid = 0 AND a.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
LEFT JOIN alerce_tap.gaiadr3_source AS g
  ON x.catid = 1 AND g.oid_catalog = x.oid_catalog
WHERE x.oid = 36028941607751853 AND x.sid = 0
```
→ 1 row(s) on 2026-11-19: catalog_name, oid_catalog, dist, w1mpro, w2mpro, w1_w2, phot_g_mean_mag, bp_rp, parallax, phot_variable_flag, in_qso_candidates

## Solar system

### Solar system · LSST

Find LSST solar-system objects, search them by orbit, and download one asteroid’s detections with Rubin’s geometry and its Minor Planet Center orbit.

**1. Look up the survey ids** (≈1 s · 3 rows)

Solar-system objects are not selected by class: they have their own survey id. sid_lut shows LSST SS Object is sid = 2 (the same telescope, tid = 1, as LSST DIA objects).


```sql
SELECT sid, tid, survey_name
FROM alerce_tap.sid_lut
ORDER BY sid
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: sid, tid, survey_name

**2. Look up bands (no features)** (≈1 s each · 6 / 0 rows)

Bands for LSST solar-system objects (sid = 2). The feature lookup returns nothing for sid = 2: light-curve features are computed for DIA objects only, so the search below uses orbital elements.

*Bands*
```sql
SELECT band, band_name, band_order
FROM alerce_tap.band
WHERE sid = 2
ORDER BY band_order
```
→ 6 row(s) on 2026-11-19: band, band_name, band_order

*Features (none for sid 2)*
```sql
SELECT feature_id, feature_name
FROM alerce_tap.feature_name_lut
WHERE sid = 2 AND feature_name IN ('Multiband_period')
```
→ 0 row(s) on 2026-11-19: feature_id, feature_name

**3. Find well-observed asteroids** (≈1 s · 10 rows)

LSST solar-system objects with the most detections. Their oid is Rubin’s ssObjectId.


```sql
SELECT TOP 10 oid, meanra, meandec, firstmjd, lastmjd, n_det
FROM alerce_tap.object
WHERE sid = 2
ORDER BY n_det DESC
```
→ 10 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, meanra, meandec, firstmjd, lastmjd, n_det

**4. Search by orbit** (≈1 s · 20 rows)

Near-Earth orbits: perihelion distance q < 1.3 au from the Minor Planet Center orbits, brightest (smallest H) first.


```sql
SELECT TOP 20 o.oid, o.n_det, m.designation, m.a, m.e, m.i, m.q, m.h
FROM alerce_tap.lsst_mpc_orbits AS m
JOIN alerce_tap.object AS o ON o.oid = m.ssobjectid AND o.sid = 2
WHERE m.q < 1.3
ORDER BY m.h
```
→ 20 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, n_det, designation, a, e, i, q, h

**5. Light curve: detections** (≈2 s · 826 rows)

Fluxes in nJy, plus the MPC designation, phase angle and solar elongation of each detection (for phase curves).


```sql
SELECT d.mjd, b.band_name, x.psfflux, x.psffluxerr,
       s.designation, s.phaseangle, s.elongation
FROM alerce_tap.detection AS d
JOIN alerce_tap.lsst_detection AS x
  ON x.oid = d.oid AND x.sid = d.sid AND x.measurement_id = d.measurement_id
JOIN alerce_tap.lsst_ss_detection AS s
  ON s.ssobjectid = d.oid AND s.measurement_id = d.measurement_id
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = d.sid AND b.band = d.band
WHERE d.oid = 21163615905265241 AND d.sid = 2
ORDER BY d.mjd
```
→ 50 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, psfflux, psffluxerr, designation, phaseangle, elongation

**6. Light curve: forced photometry** (≈1 s · 0 rows)

Forced photometry is measured at a fixed sky position, so moving objects have none: this query returns 0 rows by design.


```sql
SELECT f.mjd, b.band_name, x.psfflux, x.psffluxerr, x.scienceflux, x.sciencefluxerr
FROM alerce_tap.forced_photometry AS f
JOIN alerce_tap.lsst_forced_photometry AS x
  ON x.oid = f.oid AND x.measurement_id = f.measurement_id AND x.sid = f.sid
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE f.oid = 21163615905265241 AND f.sid = 2
ORDER BY f.mjd
```
→ 0 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, psfflux, psffluxerr, scienceflux, sciencefluxerr

**7. Crossmatch: MPC orbit** (≈1 s · 1 row)

Static catalogs (AllWISE, Gaia) do not apply to moving objects; the solar-system counterpart is the Minor Planet Center orbit, joined on ssobjectid.


```sql
SELECT designation, a, e, i, q, h, g, period, nobs_total, arc_length_total
FROM alerce_tap.lsst_mpc_orbits
WHERE ssobjectid = 21163615905265241
```
→ 1 row(s) on 2026-11-19: designation, a, e, i, q, h, g, period, nobs_total, arc_length_total

### Solar system · ZTF

Find ZTF alerts from asteroids with the stamp classifier, match them to known solar-system objects, and download one detection’s photometry.

**1. Look up the ids** (≈1 s · 6 rows)

ZTF has no separate solar-system survey id: asteroids are ZTF objects (sid = 0) that the stamp classifiers label “asteroid”. This variant uses the original ZTF stamp classifier (classifier_id = 4), class_id = 3.


```sql
SELECT s.sid, s.survey_name, c.classifier_id, c.classifier_name,
       c.classifier_version, t.class_id, t.class_name
FROM alerce_tap.classifier AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.taxonomy AS t ON t.classifier_id = c.classifier_id
JOIN alerce_tap.sid_lut AS s ON s.tid = c.tid
WHERE t.class_name IN ('asteroid')
ORDER BY s.sid, c.classifier_id, t.class_id
```
→ 6 row(s) on 2026-11-19: sid, survey_name, classifier_id, classifier_name, classifier_version, class_id, class_name

**2. Look up bands (no features)** (≈1 s each · 3 rows)

ZTF bands. Asteroid alerts are usually single detections at a given position, so light-curve features are not meaningful for them; the search below uses the known-object match in ztf_ss instead.

*Bands*
```sql
SELECT band, band_name, band_order
FROM alerce_tap.band
WHERE sid = 0
ORDER BY band_order
```
→ 3 row(s) on 2026-11-19: band, band_name, band_order

**3. Find asteroid alerts** (≈1 s · 10 rows)

Top stamp-classifier asteroid candidates with probability > 0.8.


```sql
SELECT TOP 10 p.oid, p.probability, o.meanra, o.meandec, o.firstmjd, o.lastmjd, o.n_det
FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
JOIN alerce_tap.object AS o ON o.oid = p.oid AND o.sid = p.sid
WHERE p.sid = 0 AND p.classifier_id = 4 AND p.class_id = 3
  AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
ORDER BY p.probability DESC
```
→ 10 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, meanra, meandec, firstmjd, lastmjd, n_det

**4. Search known asteroids** (≈1 s · 20 rows)

Among the top 200 asteroid candidates, keep those within 5″ of a known solar-system object (ztf_ss: name, distance and predicted magnitude from the MPC).


```sql
SELECT TOP 20 c.oid, c.probability, s.ssnamenr, s.ssdistnr, s.ssmagnr
FROM (SELECT TOP 200 p.oid, p.sid, p.probability
      FROM alerce_tap.probability AS p
      WHERE p.sid = 0 AND p.classifier_id = 4 AND p.class_id = 3
        AND p.ranking = 1 AND p.probability > 0.8
      ORDER BY p.probability DESC) AS c
JOIN alerce_tap.ztf_ss AS s ON s.oid = c.oid
WHERE s.ssdistnr < 5
ORDER BY s.ssmagnr
```
→ 20 row(s) on 2026-11-19: oid, probability, ssnamenr, ssdistnr, ssmagnr

**5. Light curve: detections** (≈1 s · 1 row)

The detection(s) of this alert. An asteroid moves, so each ZTF object usually holds a single detection.


```sql
SELECT d.mjd, b.band_name, x.magpsf, x.sigmapsf, x.magpsf_corr, x.sigmapsf_corr
FROM alerce_tap.detection AS d
JOIN alerce_tap.ztf_detection AS x
  ON x.oid = d.oid AND x.measurement_id = d.measurement_id
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = d.sid AND b.band = d.band
WHERE d.oid = 36028949647960663 AND d.sid = 0
ORDER BY d.mjd
```
→ 1 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, magpsf, sigmapsf, magpsf_corr, sigmapsf_corr

**6. Light curve: forced photometry** (≈1 s · 0 rows)

Forced photometry at the alert position. Asteroid alerts usually have none, and any that exists measures the empty sky after the object has moved on: treat it with care.


```sql
SELECT f.mjd, b.band_name, x.mag, x.e_mag, x.mag_corr, x.e_mag_corr
FROM alerce_tap.forced_photometry AS f
JOIN alerce_tap.ztf_forced_photometry AS x
  ON x.oid = f.oid AND x.measurement_id = f.measurement_id
JOIN alerce_tap.band AS b ON b.sid = f.sid AND b.band = f.band
WHERE f.oid = 36028949647960663 AND f.sid = 0
ORDER BY f.mjd
```
→ 0 row(s) on 2026-11-19: mjd, band_name, mag, e_mag, mag_corr, e_mag_corr

**7. Crossmatch: known solar-system object** (≈1 s · 1 row)

The ZTF alert’s own match to the nearest known solar-system object: name (or number), distance in arcsec and predicted magnitude.


```sql
SELECT measurement_id, ssnamenr, ssdistnr, ssmagnr
FROM alerce_tap.ztf_ss
WHERE oid = 36028949647960663
```
→ 1 row(s) on 2026-11-19: measurement_id, ssnamenr, ssdistnr, ssmagnr
